source.locator: pooling section on Pool versus Client
source.paraphrase: The driver supports both Client and Pool. Pool is useful for concurrency; a standalone Client is valid for one-off work.

invariants.why: A constructor match cannot tell a short-lived migration client from a client leaked on every request.
invariants.fixHint: Create one Pool at startup and share it. Take a dedicated client from pool.connect only for multi-statement transactions, and release it in a finally.
invariants.avoid: Exporting a single Client from a module is still one connection for every query; export a Pool instead.

source.paraphrase: Idle pool clients can error at any time, so the pool must have an error listener that observes or reports the failure instead of dropping it.

invariants.why: An empty error callback acknowledges the listener contract while swallowing the failure, so dead connections and auth breaks stay invisible until queries start failing.
invariants.fixHint: Log the error with the pool identity, or forward it to the app error reporter. Keep the handler to one call that cannot throw.
invariants.avoid: A function-expression callback with an empty body is the same swallowed error as an empty arrow.

source.paraphrase: A transaction must run on one dedicated client checked out with pool.connect. pool.query may route each statement to a different connection, which splits the transaction.

invariants.why: pool.query borrows any idle connection per call, so BEGIN, the statements, and COMMIT can land on different backends and the transaction never holds.
invariants.fixHint: Check out one client with pool.connect, run BEGIN through COMMIT on it, roll back on error, and release it in a finally.
invariants.avoid: Wrapping pool.query BEGIN in backticks or single quotes does not pin it to one connection.

source.paraphrase: pg_sleep blocks the backend for the delay. Issued from app code it parks a pooled connection that could serve real queries.

invariants.why: The sleeping backend holds its pool slot for the whole delay, so a few naps exhaust the pool and queue every other query.
invariants.fixHint: Sleep in the app with a timer between queries, or move the wait into a job queue. Keep pooled connections for statements that return promptly.
invariants.avoid: Parameterizing the delay inside a template still blocks the connection for the same seconds.

source.paraphrase: A query result carries rows as a possibly empty array. Reading a property off rows[0] assumes a row came back, which an empty result breaks.

invariants.why: An empty result makes rows[0] undefined, so the chained property read throws far from the query that returned nothing.
invariants.fixHint: Bind rows[0] to a name, throw or return early when it is missing, then read its fields. Optional chaining with a fallback also passes.
invariants.avoid: Moving the chained read inside a template still throws on zero rows; string context is not a guard.

source.paraphrase: You must always return a checked-out client to the pool, whether or not its queries failed. A client that is never released leaks, and once the pool is empty every later checkout waits forever.

invariants.why: Each unreleased client keeps one pool slot. After max leaks every request that needs the database hangs instead of failing.
invariants.fixHint: Call client.release() in a finally block after the work, passing the error when the client is broken. For one statement, use pool.query, which checks out and releases for you.
invariants.avoid: COMMIT or ROLLBACK ends the transaction, not the checkout. The rule looks for any client.release reference or a return of the client in the same file; a release reached only on the error path, or a client handed to a helper that releases it, is not judged.

source.paraphrase: A pooled client that begins a transaction must execute ROLLBACK in its catch block before client.release(), or the connection returns to the pool stuck in an open/aborted transaction.

invariants.why: Releasing a client after a failed query without issuing ROLLBACK poisons the pooled connection: every subsequent borrower hits 'current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block'.
invariants.fixHint: Add a catch (err) block that awaits client.query('ROLLBACK') and rethrows err before finally { client.release(); }.
invariants.avoid: Only try statements containing a literal BEGIN query are checked. Transactions wrapped in a reusable withTransaction(client, fn) helper only need the rollback inside that helper.
